draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Mananchira! This big pond in the middle of Kozhikode was dug as a bathing pool by the Zamorin Mana Vikrama around the 14th century, and it's fed by a natural spring. The laterite dug out of it was used to build two palaces.
draft.hungryLine: You're steps from S.M. Street, literally Sweetmeat Street, so start with something sweet.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk down S.M. Street, then on to Kozhikode Beach and the Mishkal Mosque.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Stretch out on the big lawn at Mananchira Park, with its colonial-style lamp posts and musical fountain.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Since the late 19th century, Mananchira has been kept for drinking water only. No bathing, no washing, no fun in the water.

spots.name: S. M. Street
spots.detail: 8 min walk · Kerala's busiest shopping street, with a 160 year old fire temple

spots.name: Kozhikode Beach
spots.detail: 19 min walk · Paved, lit promenade and a children's park

spots.name: Mishkal Mosque
spots.detail: 20 min walk · A wooden medieval mosque by a pond

legends.title: Tipu's gift
legends.body: It's claimed that Tipu Sultan, the Mysore ruler, turned the pond into a drinking water source as a gift for Sayed Jifri. Drinking water is still what it's kept for today.

legends.title: A thousand pillars
legends.body: Of the two temples in the Jain Derasar complex, one is said to be over 2,500 years old. It's also said to have 1,000 pillars.

tips.title: Go after 2 PM.
tips.body: The gate to Mananchira Pond and Gardens opens only in the afternoon, and it gets very crowded.

tips.title: Shoot the mosque from across the pond.
tips.body: Mishkal Mosque looks its best from the far side of its pond, and non-Muslims need special permission to go in.

story.title: A royal bath
story.body: The Zamorin Mana Vikrama had Mananchira dug as a bathing pool. The laterite from the dig built palaces to the east and west.

story.title: City of Spices
story.body: Kozhikode was one of the world's most important ports. Marco Polo, Ibn Batuta, Zheng He and Vasco da Gama all came through.

story.title: Drinking water only
story.body: The municipal council ruled the pond was for drinking only and banned bathing and washing. That rule still stands.

story.title: Gandhi Road
story.body: After Gandhi visited Kozhikode, the beach road was renamed Gandhi Road.

story.title: City of Literature
story.body: UNESCO recognised Kozhikode as India's first City of Literature. Pop into the public library by the park and you'll see why.
